overview: AutoPot is a health-gated splash healer that routes instant healing potions from the inventory into the hotbar and throws them through a rotation-gated use-item ceremony. The handler runs on the PRE stage of MotionEvent and bails while the player is flying, in creative mode, while any container window is open, or while Aura holds a target, so a throw never competes with combat rotations. findPotion scans the hotbar (slots 36-45) first and then the inventory (9-36) for splash potions carrying instant health, regeneration when the effect is not active, or move speed when the buff is missing; the heal scan only runs while health is at or below the Health threshold (default 15). The hotbar path swaps to the potion with C09, arms a throw rotation with a random 80-90 pitch via RotationUtils, waits until serverRotation.pitch reaches 80, then sends the C08 use-item packet and a C09 restore in the same tick. The inventory path refills the hotbar with a simulated open-inventory ceremony: C16 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT, a window-0 shift-click C0E, and C0D close.

sections.p: onMotion rejects the whole routine while mc.thePlayer.capabilities has allowFlying and isFlying both set, while playerController.isInCreativeMode, while msTimer.hasTimePassed(delayValue) is false (Delay 500-1000, default 500, a real period because the timer is reset after every action), while the open container's windowId differs from 0, and while Aura.target is non-null. findPotion(36, 45) walks the hotbar container range and findPotion(9, 36) the main inventory, returning the first splash potion (ItemPotion.isSplash) whose effects match the priority list: instant heal when health <= Health, regeneration when the player is not already affected, then move speed when the buff is absent. The scan returns the container index or -1, and the hotbar index for the C09 is the container index minus 36.

With a hotbar potion and no GuiInventory open, the PRE stage records potion = slot - 36 and queues C09(potion). If the current pitch is at or below 80 degrees, RotationUtils.setTargetRotation is armed with the current yaw and a pitch drawn uniformly from 80 to 90 (RandomUtils.nextFloat); the actual C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement(itemStack) fires only once RotationUtils.serverRotation.pitch has reached 80. serverRotation is refreshed from the last rotating C03/C06 the client actually sent (RotationUtils line 411), so the throw waits until the look change is on the wire rather than firing from the local aim. The single-argument C08 constructor serializes BlockPos.ORIGIN with face 255, the protocol's use-item form that routes to ItemPotion.onItemRightClick. Immediately after, C09(mc.thePlayer.inventory.currentItem) restores the held slot, potion resets to -1 and msTimer.reset() starts the cooldown. The Jump and Port modes modify the throw: onGround gates thePlayer.jump() or moveEntity(0.0, 0.42, 0.0) so the splash lands under a rising player instead of at the feet.

When a potion sits in the inventory (9-36) and the hotbar has space, the module refills it: with OpenInv on it returns unless a real GuiInventory is open, while with SimulateInventory on it fabricates the window. The fabrication sends C16PacketClientStatus(OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT), performs mc.playerController.windowClick(0, slot, 0, 1), the C0E mode-1 shift-click, and closes with C0DPacketCloseWindow. The client never renders a GUI, so the window exists only in the server's container ledger. Whether the fork's windowClick also syncs the held slot with a C09 cannot be verified here: the LiquidSense Dev snapshot ships no net/minecraft tree, so the vanilla sync contract is the only claim.

files.label: AutoPot.kt
files.explanation: The whole module: the gate chain, findPotion's heal/regen/speed scan, the C09-C08-C09 throw ceremony gated on serverRotation.pitch, and the C16-C0E-C0D simulated refill. The brief pins C08 and C09; the refill path additionally emits C0E, C16 and C0D, and the throw rides the C03 look stream via RotationUtils. The mode switch between Normal, Jump and Port only alters the local motion before the C08, never the packet shape.

files.label: RotationUtils.java (throw gate)
files.explanation: setTargetRotation stores the throw aim and the rotation system eases the server-side look toward it; serverRotation is updated only when a rotating C03/C06 is actually sent (line 411), and the module's pitch >= 80 test reads exactly that field. This is what turns a local aim into a wire-visible look change before the C08 leaves, and it is the same RotationUtils that Aura uses, which is why the module refuses to throw while Aura holds a target.

countering.label: ItemSwitchSpeed (same-tick switch after use)
countering.explanation: The direct counter to the ceremony: an InteractItemEvent from the C08 use adds the player to usedSomething, and the restore C09 arrives as an ItemSwitchEvent with currentTick - lastSwitchTick equal to 0, under the default minSwitchTicks of 1, so every throw cycle punishes. The module has no margin here: potion switch, use and restore all queue in one PRE motion tick, so raising the setting only widens the net. The check is cancelless, so the punish is pure VL accumulation.

countering.label: UseItemAdapter (face-255 use classification)
countering.explanation: The adapter classifies the throw: handleBlockPlacePacket treats any pre-1.9 face index above 5, and the single-argument C08 serializes face 255, so data.mightUseItem is set. Every C09, both the potion-in and the restore, hits onChangeSlot and calls requestItemUseResync, forcibly releasing the server-side item use each cycle. The honest gap: splash potions skip setItemInUse at the pre-1.9 durability guard (> 16384), so the consume half never registers and the pressure is the resync churn rather than a completion ledger.

countering.label: FastConsume (splash completion gap)
countering.explanation: NCP stamps the consume start on a consumable right-click and completes it on PlayerItemConsumeEvent, which a splash throw never fires, so only the start half of the ledger engages. The restore C09 resets the ledger through onItemHeldChange on every cycle, so the module churns the stamp without ever violating the interval. This entry is an honest boundary: FastConsume cannot see the throw complete, and the module's real exposure stays in the C0E refill and movement layers.

countering.label: PacketListener (soup-gated inventory feed)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's HELD_ITEM_SLOT and BLOCK_PLACE handlers are both gated on Material.MUSHROOM_SOUP, so the potion C09 and the face-255 C08 bypass the AutoHeal inventory feed entirely; the InventoryListener stamps consumeTime for POTION right-clicks, but FastConsume compares it on PlayerItemConsumeEvent, which splash throws never produce. The potion throw is invisible to Arc v2's inventory layer by construction, and its movement layer is where any real pressure would have to come from.
